$schema: AXP Africa Design System — extracted for app development

meta.name: AXP Africa
meta.northStar: The Trusted Ledger — a well-kept institutional record: navy and gold, hairline rules, generous margins, quiet confidence rather than sales pressure.
antiPatterns: gold used as a large fill or body-text color

color.usageRule: The One Signal Rule: gold marks small deliberate points of attention (eyebrows, one button variant, focus rings, active-nav underline, the ring emblem). It never fills a large surface or colors body text. Navy is the dominant surface/brand color.

navy.usage: Dominant surface color — hero backgrounds, primary buttons, headline text, dark section bands, sidebar.

navyInk.usage: Text-on-gold (gold button label), darkest surface tone, dark form panels.

gold.usage: Eyebrow labels, gold button variant, focus-visible outlines, active/hover nav underline, decorative ring emblem. Reserved and rare by design.

goldLight.usage: Eyebrow labels on navy/dark backgrounds, for legibility.

alabasterPaper.usage: Warm off-white for bounded 'quiet' section backgrounds and the mobile nav panel. Distinct from and warmer than the default canvas.

ledgerSlate.usage: Secondary body-text color used for section/feature/story copy. Close variants (#4f5564, #515665, #606574) appear in nav and micro-labels — treat as one family.

surfaceCanvas.usage: Default page/body background for the functional (app/form) UI layer.

surfaceBorder.usage: Functional-component border/input stroke (distinct from hand-authored hairline navy borders).

destructive.usage: Validation/error red — forms, alerts, functional UI only. Never part of the marketing palette.

reservedUnused.note: Present as CSS variables but not adopted anywhere in the app. Do not use without an explicit design decision.

darkMode.note: Only defined for the shadcn/functional component layer (dashboards, forms) — marketing pages are light-mode only.

typography.usageRule: The One-Voice-Per-Job Rule: Lora is exclusively for emotional/display headlines; Poppins is exclusively for everything functional (body, labels, nav, buttons). Never mix roles.

display.usage: Page-hero H1s only — the single largest statement on a page.

headline.usage: Section H2s throughout the app. Canonical — consolidate new headings here rather than inventing new clamp ranges.

lead.usage: The one enlarged intro paragraph directly under a hero or section headline.

label.usage: Eyebrows, button text, nav links, badges — the busiest type role in the system.

radius.usageRule: The Square-Precision Rule: anything directly actionable (buttons, menu items) stays near-square (3px). Anything a compact status marker goes fully pill (999px). Nothing in between in the marketing vocabulary. The functional/app layer (cards, dialogs, forms) uses a rounder, more conventional scale.

elevation.usageRule: The Hover-Lift Rule: depth responds to interaction, not resting decoration. Cards rise -5px and shadow deepens on hover; never a static heavy shadow at rest.

rest.usage: Baseline elevation for cards/frames at rest.

soft.usage: Hover response for cards, frames, interactive grid items.

deep.usage: Floating chrome above page content — nav overflow dropdowns, overlays.

interactiveFast.usage: Button/link color, transform, border-color transitions on hover/focus.

cardLift.usage: Card/frame transform and box-shadow transition on hover.

heroBreathe.usage: Slow ambient zoom on hero background photography (scale 1.06 to 1).

motion.reducedMotion: Always respect prefers-reduced-motion — disable non-essential animation and cap transition durations at .01ms.
motion.library: Framer Motion vocabulary (fadeInUp, staggerContainer/staggerItem, springPresets) via @/lib/motion — reuse instead of inventing new easing/timing.

breakpoints.note: No dedicated tablet tier beyond these two steps.

focusState.usage: Applied uniformly to buttons, nav links, and form controls on focus-visible.

secondary_gold.note: The only variant that inverts to dark-on-light label.

glass.usage: Over photography or navy hero surfaces.

button.disabled: opacity: .45, cursor: not-allowed — fade only, no color change

badge_chip.usage: Small meta markers only — e.g. flagging illustrative/placeholder content ('prototype-note'). Never used for buttons or cards.

input.focus: same gold 2px outline / 3px offset as buttons

link.activeHover: gold 2px underline slides in from left; color shifts to full navy

mobile.linkTypography: serif display, 19px/500 — the one navigational use of the display font

eyebrowLabel.usage: Primary wayfinding device — opens nearly every major section.

signatureEmblem.name: Circular Gold-Ring Emblem
signatureEmblem.description: Large (~680px) thin gold-stroke circle with 1-2 soft glow rings, bled off the top-right corner of dark navy surfaces only.
signatureEmblem.constraint: Never on light backgrounds, never carries content, max once per section.

layoutPatterns.section: 112px vertical padding, alternating bands: default canvas / navy / alabaster
layoutPatterns.featureSplit: asymmetric two-column, 1.08fr/.92fr, 95px gap, collapses to 1 column under 900px
layoutPatterns.splitHeading: heading left + supporting link/action right, 50px gap

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Gold never fills a large surface or colors body text — it always marks a small, deliberate point of attention.

rules.name: The One-Voice-Per-Job Rule
rules.body: Lora is exclusively for emotional/display headlines; Poppins is exclusively for everything functional. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Hover-Lift Rule
rules.body: Depth is a response to interaction, not a resting decoration. A card's shadow always deepens and the card always rises -5px on hover — never the reverse.

rules.name: The Square-Precision Rule
rules.body: Actionable elements stay near-square (3px). Compact status markers go fully pill (999px). Nothing in between in the marketing vocabulary.

doNotUse: Gold as a card/section/button fill or body-text color
Urgency patterns: countdown badges, saturated gradient CTAs, stacked photo carousels as hero
New headline clamp() ranges — consolidate onto the canonical headline token
The unused --axp-blue / --axp-green / --axp-orange tokens without an explicit adoption decision
